paper_section: Official C03 §3, PDF pp.3–4; §5.1/Figure 2, p.6; supplement Tables 12–14 and §9; supplied tabllm.pdf corroborates definitions.
compared_conditions: List Template vs List Permuted Names
claim_text: The same applies to the list serialization with permuted feature names. content_claim_quote: The same applies to the list serialization with permuted feature names. [...] TabLLM [...] also relies on the association of the names with the correct values.
content_claim_rationale: Permuting names leaves both names and values in the prompt and changes only the pairing; the authors interpret the drop as reliance on the correct name–value association, i.e. intended vs altered content.
utility_claim_quote: TabLLM relies on information from the feature names in the zero-shot and few-shot regime, and also relies on the association of the names with the correct values.
utility_claim_rationale: The interpretation offered is reliance/dependence in the zero- and few-shot regime; no claim that the semantic information yields a predictive performance gain (the authors stress that performance equalizes with more examples).
content_support_rationale: The list template, the values and their order are unchanged; only the column name attached to each value is permuted, and the same permutation is applied to every example. Model (T0), T-Few fine-tuning and evaluation are identical.
utility_support_rationale: Removal fails: the names stay in the serialization and are merely misassigned, so the comparator represents wrong content rather than absent content.
construction_evidence: TabLLM §3.2: List Permuted Names is the List Template with permuted column names, so each value carries the wrong name; the permutation is fixed across all examples.

paper_section: Official C03 §3, PDF pp.3–4; §5.1/Figure 2, p.6; supplement Tables 12–14 and §9; supplied tabllm.pdf corroborates definitions.
compared_conditions: List Template vs List Only Values
claim_text: Using only feature values had a poor performance for zero and very few shots, but the performance equalized with more training examples. The same applies to the list serialization with permuted feature names. This indicates that if enough training examples are available, the serialization approach does not matter, but that TabLLM relies on information from the feature names in the zero-shot and few-shot regime, and also relies on the association of the names with the correct values.
content_claim_quote: TabLLM relies on information from the feature names in the zero-shot and few-shot regime, and also relies on the association of the names with the correct values.
content_claim_rationale: Only-Values removes the column names entirely, and the corresponding claim ("relies on information from the feature names") is a presence/absence statement, not a claim about which names are used.
utility_claim_quote: Using only feature values had a poor performance for zero and very few shots, but the performance equalized with more training examples.
utility_claim_rationale: The performance difference is reported descriptively and interpreted as low-shot reliance plus equalization; the authors do not frame it as semantic knowledge improving prediction. Consistent with the prior adjudication that all three TabLLM comparisons make no utility claim.
content_support_rationale: The column names are deleted outright (values only), a presence/absence manipulation with no altered-content arm.
utility_support_rationale: Removal: column names are dropped. Preservation: all feature values remain, in the fixed column order, so the field–value binding survives positionally. Interface: same serialization pipeline, same T0 model and T-Few fine-tuning. Caveat for the second coder: whether positional-only binding counts as preserved field structure is the decision point here.
construction_evidence: TabLLM §3.2: List Only Values applies the List Template to the feature values alone, to test whether column names aid performance.

paper_section: Official C03 §3, PDF pp.3–4; §5.1/Figure 2, p.6; supplement Tables 12–14 and §9; supplied tabllm.pdf corroborates definitions.
compared_conditions: List Template vs List Permuted Values
claim_text: The discrepancy for zero and very few shots was even stronger for List Permuted Values, which suggests that TabLLM relies more on the correct values than feature names. Again, the performance equalized for more examples showing the ability of TabLLM to learn new associations if enough training data is available.
content_claim_quote: The discrepancy for zero and very few shots was even stronger for List Permuted Values, which suggests that TabLLM relies more on the correct values than feature names.
content_claim_rationale: Values remain present but are replaced by altered surface forms; the claim is about reliance on the correct values, i.e. dependence on the particular content.
utility_claim_quote: Again, the performance equalized for more examples showing the ability of TabLLM to learn new associations if enough training data is available.
utility_claim_rationale: Interpreted as reliance and as learnability of new associations, not as a demonstration that semantic content improves predictive performance.
content_support_rationale: Beyond the semantic manipulation, the comparator also changes the granularity of the data: continuous values are discretized into ten uniform bins before the per-column permutation is applied, while the base List Template carries the raw values. Predictive information other than semantic content therefore changes as well, so the contrast does not isolate content sensitivity. For purely categorical datasets the same construction would be a clean content control.
utility_support_rationale: Removal fails (values are altered, not removed) and Preservation fails for continuous features because of the ten-bin discretization.
construction_evidence: TabLLM §3.2: List Permuted Values applies one fixed per-column permutation to all values; for continuous values ten uniform bins are used.
